entities.name: Battle of the Camel
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of the Camel, fought on November 10, 656, was a pivotal event in the First Fitna, the civil war that ravaged the Rashidun Caliphate after the death of Prophet Muhammad. This conflict at Basra pitted the Uthman ibn Affan loyalists against the supporters of Ali ibn Abi Talib, marking a significant turning point in the struggle for power within the Muslim community.

The battle was a brutal clash between the two factions, with both sides suffering heavy losses. Estimates suggest that the casualties numbered in the thousands, with the size of the armies involved likely ranging between 5,000 to 10,000 men. The defeat of the Uthman ibn Affan loyalists at the Battle of the Camel paved the way for the eventual triumph of Ali's forces, who would go on to claim the caliphate.

The consequences of this battle were far-reaching, shaping the future of the Islamic world and setting in motion the chain of events that would lead to the eventual downfall of the Rashidun Caliphate. The legacy of the Battle of the Camel can be seen in the ongoing sectarian divisions within the Islamic world, with the conflict's impact still felt today.

As Ali ibn Abi Talib himself noted, 'The Battle of the Camel was a trial by fire, a test of the mettle of the Muslim community, and one that would ultimately reveal the true nature of its leaders.' The event's significance extends beyond the realm of Islamic history, serving as a powerful reminder of the enduring power of conflict to shape the course of human civilization.
